question: Do authentic staff/patient/event photos outperform designed graphics, organically?
scope: Santiam Hospital & Clinics Facebook page + Instagram, posts only (Stories excluded)
window_note: Meta's Content table stops serving rows at ~200; 193 posts were retrievable in one view, which reaches back to Mar 18. The channel-level ledger still covers the full Jan 1 - Aug 31 period.
method: Every post's creative thumbnail was viewed and hand-classified into one of three buckets. Metrics are ORGANIC ONLY: Meta reports a 'from ads' portion for both reach and reactions on boosted posts, and that portion is subtracted. Classification is a manual visual judgement, not a Meta field.

buckets.photo: Authentic photo - real staff, patients, events, facilities. Little or no graphic overlay.
buckets.provider: Provider portrait card - a real staff headshot placed in a branded template (Welcome / Provider Spotlight).
buckets.graphic: Designed graphic - heavy text and layout, stock imagery, illustration, event flyers, awareness-month creative.

headline_findings: Authentic photos earn 3.8x the median organic reactions of designed graphics (15 vs 4).
Authentic photos reach 1.3x more people at the median (511 vs 393) and 2.2x at the mean (1,296 vs 586).
Authentic photos are only 23% of output; designed graphics are 70%.
Boost money flows the wrong way: 64% of graphics were boosted vs 35% of photos.

COUNTERPOINT, kept deliberately: designed graphics earn MORE shares per post (2.31 vs 1.35). Event and announcement graphics are built to be forwarded, and that is a real strength - the share is the call to action.
